name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 GSQ-RCO Coder (ISTA-DASLab)

lineage.how_derived: 192 of 384 routed experts per layer removed by RCO (KL minimization on calibration data incl. SVG and three.js), remaining experts at the IQ2_XXS quant types (about 1 bit per transformer parameter)

purpose: ISTA states: a compressed DeepSeek V4.1 Flash aimed at code and agentic workflows, long context and vision; unpruned releases recommended for general use; release experimental.

license.name: MIT (inherited from the base)
license.notes: Base repo deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 LICENSE read: standard MIT ("to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell copies"). The ISTA GGUF repo has no LICENSE file; its card states the weights inherit the base license and the GSQ-RCO tooling is under its repository license (not read).

architecture.kind: sparse MoE with MQA, compressed KV, top-512 indexer, hyper-connections and Engram lookup tables
architecture.why_this_design: Not restated by ISTA; the base vendor's architecture (research/49). Pruned file keeps 280.1 B transformer parameters and 196.6 B Engram parameters.

variants.format: GGUF, transformer 72.12 GB in 5 shards plus Engram 110.60 GB (SSD) plus mmproj 0.97 GB
variants.notes: Engram table is read one row per token from disk

pc-12gb.notes: estimate from the file size (72.1 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 9.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 60 GB; about 13% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that); plus 110.6 GB Engram table read from SSD

pc-16gb.notes: estimate from the file size (72.1 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 13.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 64 GB; about 19% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that); plus 110.6 GB Engram table read from SSD

pc-24gb.notes: estimate from the file size (72.1 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 21.6 GB VRAM plus 82 GB RAM = 104 GB; about 30% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that); plus 110.6 GB Engram table read from SSD

pc-32gb.notes: estimate from the file size (72.1 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 29.6 GB VRAM plus 114 GB RAM = 144 GB; about 41% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that); plus 110.6 GB Engram table read from SSD

mac-16-24gb.notes: estimate from the file size (72.1 GB) against the GPU share of docs/hardware (about 12 GB); plus 110.6 GB Engram table read from SSD

mac-32gb.notes: estimate from the file size (72.1 GB) against the GPU share of docs/hardware (about 22 GB); plus 110.6 GB Engram table read from SSD

mac-64gb+.notes: estimate from the file size (72.1 GB) against the GPU share of docs/hardware (about 52 GB); plus 110.6 GB Engram table read from SSD

engine_support.notes: card: llama.cpp b11870 or newer; research/49 found two cards disagreeing on support

strengths: Strongest coding evidence of anything within reach of 32 GB VRAM plus 128 GB RAM (research/49 ranking)
weaknesses: Multi-step agentic tasks lose more than single-problem code (maker)
182 GB on disk, 110 GB Engram on fast storage
Capabilities outside the calibration mix degrade
soft.behavior: Effort level 50 in the vendor benchmark.

tona_fit.reason: Best coding evidence (vendor LiveCodeBench 88.6) for the 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM class, MIT text verified. Judged for its users, not for what Tona runs today; 72 GB resident plus 110 GB Engram on SSD does not fit the 16 GB + 64 GB class.
blockers: Tona has no DeepSeek-V4 module (MQA, indexer, hyper-connections, Engram): engine support, not quality

sources.note: page text read through a summarizer (WebFetch)
